extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and interested parties who want to submit comments on USDA AMS proposed rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for members of the public on how to submit and what to include when commenting on USDA Agricultural Marketing Service proposed rules, plus how comments are considered in the agency's rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to Submit Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Public feedback to notices open for comment is gathered via www.regulations.gov. Comments are more often submitted to an agency through www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments through regulations.gov (the page identifies this as the common/primary channel for agency comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Please include your full name and mailing address (street, city, state and zip code) with your comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include complete personal contact details with each comment; the page specifies full name and full mailing address components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices, except for final rules, are open for public comment until the deadline stated within the notice. Comment periods include weekends and holidays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission means by the date stated in the notice; for example, if a 60-day period closes on Saturday, submissions on the following Monday are untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may comment and scope of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice-and-comment process enables anyone to submit a comment on any part of a proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no limitation described on who may submit or which parts of the proposed rule may be addressed—individuals, organizations, and other stakeholders may comment on any element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking record standard (what the agency must consider)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency must base its conclusions on the rulemaking record, consisting of the comments, scientific data, expert opinions, and facts accumulated during the pre-rule and proposed rule stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that supply data, expert opinion, or factual information become part of the rulemaking record and are considered when the agency reaches conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: What makes a comment potentially influential
rubrics_metrics.description: If the rulemaking record contains persuasive new data or sound policy arguments, the agency may decide to terminate the rulemaking, or to continue the rulemaking but change aspects of the rule to reflect these new issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To affect the final rule, provide persuasive new evidence or well-reasoned policy arguments; purely duplicative or unsupported assertions are less likely to change agency conclusions.
